newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends bit firmer on forex inflow.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends bit firmer on forex inflow.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed marginally firmer at 26.373 to the dollar as modest inflows of foreign exchange prompted some banks to sell their dollar holdings, traders said.
On Wednesday, the peso closed at 26.374 on Wednesday.
A total of $283 million changed hands on Thursday, but most of the deals were either settled today and on Monday.
Based on the Philippine market convention, trades done today are settled the next day.
"It seems that nobody wants to deal value-tomorrow. Most of the trades are valued-today or valued spot," one trader said.
Value-spot deals are trades settled after two working days. He said traders decided to play the arbitrage game one day earlier.
Usually, arbitraging traders take advantage of the swap points earned over the weekend on Fridays. "They just decided to do the arbitraging a day earlier," one trader said.
The peso was being dealt at 26.369 for value-today, and at 26.289/26.390 for value spot. Done rates were not captured in the Philippine Dealing System.
The Central Bank kept its dollar offering price at 26.375.
